# Monocular depth models (one image)

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

33 depth models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 994x1482: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured. The accuracy column is lower-is-better (NYUv2 AbsRel (scale+shift aligned)).

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## Depth Anything 3

Commercial use: `da3mono-large`, `da3metric-large`: yes; `da3-large-1.1`, `da3-giant-1.1`, `da3nested-giant-large-1.1`: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

### Limitations

- Metric checkpoints predict at most max_depth (20 m Hypersim, 80 m Virtual KITTI 2): the head is a sigmoid scaled by it. Each was fine-tuned on one synthetic domain, so indoor / outdoor scenes outside it get a wrong scale.
- Distill-Any-Depth runs with this family's pipeline (short side 518, aspect kept, as the authors' transformers ports); the authors' demo squashes to 700 x 700. Their Dav2-Teacher-Large-2w-iter checkpoint is not included.

- Variants: `video-depth-anything-s`, `video-depth-anything-metric-s`
- Outputs: inverse_depth, depth; kind: `affine_invariant_inverse`
- Input size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `video-depth-anything-s` not measured yet; `video-depth-anything-metric-s` not measured yet
- `video-depth-anything-s` 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 83 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `video-depth-anything-s` original 1080x1920: upstream infer_video_depth(input_size=518, fp32=False): uint8 numpy frames in, numpy out (its API); the authors' autocast fp16
- `video-depth-anything-s` portable 1080x1920, kernels 1080x1920: float CUDA frames in [0, 1] in, depth [L, H, W] on the device out
- `video-depth-anything-s` load / first call: original 0.26 s / 14.043 s (1080x1920), portable 0.18 s / 1.455 s (1080x1920), kernels 0.12† s / 1.301 s (1080x1920)
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, one video per call (4 windows of 32 frames), first call, 1 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3; ms per video
- Speed and memory not measured for: `video-depth-anything-metric-s`.

### Measured

AbsRel / delta1 after a least-squares scale + shift fit (in disparity space for inverse-depth models), mean over images. Video: one call per sequence, one scale + shift per sequence, AbsRel / delta1 over all its pixels with Kinect depth, mean over sequences. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `video-depth-anything-s` | TUM RGB-D video (3 sequences, first 110 frames each), AbsRel / delta1 | 0.0549 / 0.9802 | 0.0549 / 0.9802 | 0.0550 / 0.9802 | 0.0549 / 0.9802 |  |
| `video-depth-anything-s` | TUM RGB-D video (3 sequences, first 1000 frames each), AbsRel / delta1 |  |  |  | 0.1120 / 0.8716 |  |
| `video-depth-anything-metric-s` | TUM RGB-D video (3 sequences, first 110 frames each), AbsRel / delta1 | 0.0786 / 0.9769 | 0.0785 / 0.9769 | 0.0786 / 0.9769 | 0.0785 / 0.9769 |  |
| `video-depth-anything-metric-s` | TUM RGB-D video (3 sequences, first 1000 frames each), AbsRel / delta1 |  |  |  | 0.1214 / 0.8883 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks a49aaba7, 2026-11-12.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.42 % and p99 <= 0.55 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `inverse_depth`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `video-depth-anything-s` | 0.00042 / 0.00105 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |
| `video-depth-anything-metric-s` | 0.00273 / 0.00361 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fastbb@7d058322634d:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- A call's batch is one video in time order: frames are not independent (each window attends over time and is aligned to the previous one), so a batch is not the same as single calls.
- Every call runs at least one 32-frame window (shorter videos are padded with copies of their last frame): one image costs about as much as 32 frames in the temporal head.
- The whole video's depth is kept on the device as float32 (L x H x W); split very long videos.

</details>

## ZoeDepth

ZoeDepth from the Intelligent Systems Lab: metric depth from one image, for indoor and outdoor scenes.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zoedepth-nk` | Middlebury 2014 half (994x1482) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 408<br>271<br>124<br>88.9<br>71.7<br>73.3 | 3897 / 3948<br>2040 / 2146<br>2037 / 2124<br>1771 / 1960<br>1813 / 1880<br>2246 / 2306 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/isl-org/ZoeDepth> at `d87f17b`
- Code licence: MIT (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: MIT (assumed from code)
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/isl-org/ZoeDepth/blob/d87f17b2f5fdcb174cf4fb115491f4a6c60de152/LICENSE (weights are release assets of the same repository)
- Training data: MiDaS v3.1 BEiT-L relative-depth pre-training on 12 datasets, then metric fine-tuning on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI (ZoeDepth paper, arXiv 2302.12288)
- Options: `pad_input` = True, `flip` = True
- Kernel libraries: `cudnn_hacc`
- Variants: `zoedepth-nk`
- Outputs: depth; kind: `metric`
- Input size: any H x W >= 8, resized or padded inside the model
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `zoedepth-nk` 3000x4000 (2.4 GiB peak allocated, 2.6 reserved)
- `zoedepth-nk` 994x1482, first call: portable + torch.compile 94 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 138 s (ONNX + engine).
- `zoedepth-nk` original 994x1482: torch.autocast(fp16) around the forward
- `zoedepth-nk` load / first call: original 8.35 s / 1.528 s, portable 1.92 s / 0.275 s, kernels 0.33† s / 0.122 s
- † measured in the speed sweep after the portable load (or an earlier size) in the same process: file cache and kernels are warm, so the time is lower than a fresh start.
- Protocol, median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input (synthetic for bench_inputs sizes), card defaults; gc before each load; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

### Measured

AbsRel / delta1 after a least-squares scale + shift fit (in disparity space for inverse-depth models), mean over images. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `zoedepth-nk` | iBims-1, AbsRel / delta1 | 0.0669 / 0.9545 | 0.0668 / 0.9546 (NaN / inf output) | 0.0669 / 0.9545 | 0.0669 / 0.9545 |  |
| `zoedepth-nk` | ETH3D two-view train left, AbsRel / delta1 | 0.1139 / 0.8648 | 0.1130 / 0.8653 (NaN / inf output) | 0.1139 / 0.8647 | 0.1139 / 0.8648 | possibly in the training data |
| `zoedepth-nk` | Middlebury 2014 trainingH left, AbsRel / delta1 | 0.0449 / 0.9860 | 0.0449 / 0.9860 | 0.0449 / 0.9860 | 0.0449 / 0.9860 | possibly in the training data |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 939adfe8, 2026-11-06.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 1 % and p99 <= 3 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zoedepth-nk` | 0.00045 / 0.00078 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `cudnn_hacc@cudnn92400` |

### Limitations

- torch.compile(fullgraph=True) and torch.export are not supported: graph break in the vendored MiDaS core call and data-dependent NYU / KITTI head routing (documented xfail).
- Inputs below 5 px per side raise InputError when pad_input is on.
